name: Suricata Operations — Config, File Extraction & Ruleset Management
description: Suricata operational tasks: validating configuration (-T), managing rules (suricata-update, live reload via SIGUSR2), enabling file extraction (file-store in suricata.yaml + filestore rule), and inspecting extracted files (SHA256-named, organized by first 2 chars of hash). Key commands for ruleset management: list-sources, enable-source, suricata-update. Live reload avoids restart downtime.
notes:
=== VALIDATE CONFIGURATION ===
sudo suricata -T -c /etc/suricata/suricata.yaml
  → Runs test mode: checks config file + all referenced files
  → Output: 'Configuration provided was successfully loaded. Exiting.'
  → No traffic processing — just config validation

=== ADD LOCAL RULES ===
# 1. Create /home/htb-student/local.rules with rule
# 2. Edit suricata.yaml:
sudo vim /etc/suricata/suricata.yaml

  rule-files:
    - suricata.rules
    - local.rules        ← add this line

# 3. Verify rules loaded:
ls -lah /etc/suricata/rules/
more /etc/suricata/rules/emerging-malware.rules

=== LIVE RULE RELOADING ===
# In suricata.yaml:
detect-engine:
  - reload: true

# Then signal the running process to reload rules:
sudo kill -usr2 $(pidof suricata)
  → Reloads ruleset WITHOUT restarting Suricata
  → No traffic gap during reload

=== UPDATING RULESETS ===
# Simple update (Emerging Threats Open by default):
sudo suricata-update
  → Fetches from https://rules.emergingthreats.net/open/
  → Saves to /var/lib/suricata/rules/suricata.rules
  → Tests with suricata -T after update

# List available ruleset providers:
sudo suricata-update list-sources
  → et/open (Proofpoint, MIT)
  → et/pro (Proofpoint, Commercial)
  → oisf/trafficid (OISF, MIT)
  → sslbl/ssl-fp-blacklist (Abuse.ch, Non-Commercial)
  → sslbl/ja3-fingerprints (Abuse.ch JA3 hashes)
  → tgreen/hunting (threat hunting rules, GPLv3)
  → malsilo/win-malware (commodity malware, MIT)

# Enable a specific ruleset source:
sudo suricata-update enable-source et/open
sudo suricata-update   ← then re-run update to pull new source

# Restart Suricata after major ruleset changes:
sudo systemctl restart suricata

=== FILE EXTRACTION ===
# 1. Edit suricata.yaml:
file-store:
  version: 2
  enabled: yes
  force-filestore: yes  ← store ALL files (not just rule-triggered)
  dir: /var/log/suricata/filestore  ← default location

# 2. Add extraction rule to local.rules:
alert http any any -> any any (msg:"FILE store all"; filestore; sid:2; rev:1;)
  → This rule triggers file extraction for ALL HTTP transferred files

# 3. Run Suricata:
suricata -r /home/htb-student/pcaps/vm-2.pcap
  → Creates: eve.json, fast.log, stats.log, suricata.log, filestore/

# 4. Inspect extracted files:
cd filestore
find . -type f
  → Files named by SHA256 hash
  → Organized: filestore/XX/XXHASH... (first 2 chars of SHA256 = subdir)
  → Example: f9bc6d... → filestore/f9/f9bc6d...

# 5. Inspect file content:
xxd ./21/21742fc621f83041db2e47b0899f5aea6caa00a4b67dbff0aae823e6817c5433 | head
  → MZ header = Windows PE executable
  → Look for file magic bytes to identify type
